title: Budgeting Basics for Your First Job
summary: Learn how to manage your money with a budget, track your spending, and save for your goals.

sections.heading: Why Budget?
sections.body: A budget is a plan for your money. It helps you see where your money is going and make sure you have enough for what's important. With inflation around 5.2% a year, your money's buying power can decrease, making a budget even more crucial.

sections.heading: Tracking Your Spending
sections.body: The first step is to track where your money goes. Use your bank account statements, UPI transactions, or a simple notebook. Knowing your spending habits helps you identify areas where you can save.

sections.heading: Saving for Goals
sections.body: Once you know your spending, you can set savings goals. A bank savings account offers safety and instant access, though it earns only about 2.7% interest. For longer-term goals, consider options like a Recurring Deposit/Fixed Deposit (FD) offering around 6.5% or a SIP in a Nifty 50 index fund, which has historically averaged around 11% but carries medium risk.

example.title: Rohan's First Budget
example.body: Rohan just got his first job and earns ₹30,000 per month. He decides to create a budget. He allocates ₹10,000 for rent, ₹5,000 for food and transport, ₹3,000 for fun, and ₹2,000 for family support, as his parents need money for his sibling's education. This leaves him with ₹10,000. He decides to put ₹5,000 into a Recurring Deposit and ₹5,000 into a SIP for his future goals.

takeaway: A budget helps you control your money, save for the future, and avoid debt.
